subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - next steps

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure I captured your priorities and next steps. Please reply/edit if I missed anything.

Pain points you called out:
- Rising cost and unpredictable per-token spend on current OpenAI usage (especially for high-throughput inference).
- Concerns about vendor lock-in and wanting the flexibility to run on dedicated/private infra.
- Latency variability for streaming-style features in production (user-facing chat + summarization).
- Compliance: need audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.

Current stack you shared:
- Production: OpenAI (gpt-4.1) for chat and generations; Anthropic for a small reranking flow.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for vector search (daily batch reindex).
- Host: AWS (us-west-2) with microservices on ECS and Postgres for metadata.

Success criteria for migration:
- Match or improve latency and per-request cost vs current OpenAI baseline.
- Seamless API compatibility or small SDK shim so product teams need minimal code changes.
- Private deployment option (VPC) for sensitive pipelines; ability to pin model versions.
- Audit logs, KMS integration, and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial):
- Mistral, Llama-3 family, Meta's Llama 2 variants (quantized where feasible) for generation.
- Open models with strong embedding-replacement lineage for current OpenAI embedding use.
- Redwood to run compatibility checks and perf profiles vs your sample workloads.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive: 60-minute session with your infra and SRE (Ben?) + our SE (Rishi) to go over traffic patterns, seq lengths, and latency SLOs.
2) Share your sample production prompts, traffic distribution, and a redacted dataset for perf/quality checks (we'll sign an NDA if required).
3) Redwood will run an initial cost/latency estimate and a 2-week pilot plan (Dedicated or Private) with a model shortlist.
4) Procurement checklist: I attached a one-page MAP and our SSO/KMS checklist for review.

Suggested times for deep-dive: Tue 2027-02-02 14:00 or Wed 2027-02-03 10:00 PT — tell me what works and I’ll lock in the invite.

Thanks again — excited to help you reduce costs and remove the lock-in risk.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (1.2MB)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Jacobs <ben.j@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 19:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the succinct recap, that's accurate. A couple clarifications:
- Cost detail: our main pain is inference tokens on chat sessions (peak concurrency around 400 DCUs) — we currently pay for streaming tokens that spike during our daily reports.
- Embeddings: we use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; quality must be within ~2% of current MRR impact for retrieval relevance.
- Compliance: Procurement needs SOC 2 Type II and proof of KMS integration.

Ben will join the technical deep-dive; he's our infra lead and can share traffic patterns. Wed 2027-02-03 10:00 PT works best for us.

We'll prepare a small set of redacted prompts and a sample batch of embeddings for your perf tests.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product | Acme Analytics
alyssa@acmeanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 19:20:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - next steps

Rishi / Aditya — forwarding Alyssa's confirmation. Key asks:
- Perf target: match current OpenAI latency under peak concurrency (~400 DCUs).
- Embedding quality tolerance: within ~2% of current retrieval quality (we'll get a labeled set).
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II + KMS evidence required for procurement.

Can you run through our suggested shortlist (Mistral, Llama-3 family, quantized Llama-2 variants) and prepare an initial perf checklist for the Wed 10:00 PT call? Also please flag any blockers for a Private deployment in their AWS account (VPC peering, KMS keys).

I attached the MAP we shared with them.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: redwood-sso-integration-checklist.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap / scheduling deep-dive (Acme Analytics)

Hi all —

Thanks Marissa and Alyssa — Wed 2027-02-03 10:00 PT is booked on my calendar and I sent the invite. Agenda I'll cover:
1) Traffic profile and sequence length distribution (please share 24-72h p95/p99 if possible).
2) Embedding replacement plan and evaluation criteria (we'll run an A/B on a labeled subset).
3) Pilot options: Dedicated vs Private (pros/cons, timeline, infra requirements).
4) Procurement checklist & SOC 2 evidence pack we can share ahead of procurement call.

Requesting before the call:
- Redacted prompt set + sample embeddings (S3 link or HubSpot attachment).
- Current p95/p99 latency metrics for chat generation and streaming tail behavior.
- Any firewall/VPC constraints or third-party compliance requirements.

I'll prepare model perf profiles and a cost estimate matrix for the shortlist. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
